## Method and limits
- Windows: both calls cover 2017–2025 [c1][c2]. The latest dated record seen is 2025-10-30 [r1], which is 358 days before today (2026-10-23). 2025 may be incomplete, and nothing from 2026 is covered. The corpus starts in 2017 [c2], so earlier debate is invisible.
- Lane: research papers only. No news or policy documents were queried.
- Coverage: the index passed its row checks, though the tool says this is "not an ingest completeness proof" [c1][c2].
- Unexplained discrepancy: the trend call tallies 328 labelled papers [c1], while the browse facet labels 753 [c2]. Cautionary is 33 in one [c1] and 54 in the other [c2]. The whole-subject contested share is 82.6% [c2], against about 30% yearly in [c1]. I cannot tell which papers [c1] omits. Levels are therefore not comparable across the two calls, and the trend rests only on [c1]'s internal consistency. If the omitted papers differ systematically by year, the trend could change.
- Censoring: in the 2017 row of [c1], orientation labels cover 30 of 40 papers, and the 2018 row covers 22 of 47. The contested share uses all papers as denominator, so unlabelled papers pull it down in those years.
- Match mode: phrase match on title and keywords, with expansion off (expand=false) [c2]. Four phrases were matched. "ai-enabled weapons" has 2 title hits and "autonomous lethal systems" has 0 [c2]. Broader military-AI topics such as targeting, decision support and cyber were not captured, and results could change if the concept cluster were expanded.
- What the counts are: papers whose own framing was machine-labelled. They are not evidence about whether claims are true or whether policy has become more cautious. The tool warns that orientation is "how a paper frames its own finding, not a verdict" [c1].
- Interpretation (mine): the roughly one-point share gains for cautionary and critical are within what small cells can produce, so I read them as a possible mild shift and not a finding.
- Cannot answer: whether the broader military-AI field (beyond autonomous weapons) is more cautionary; whether the shift differs by region or discipline; and which specific critical papers underlie the 2025 jump.
